methodology.playerValueCurve: v(adp) = 100 * exp(-0.028 * (adp - 1)); floor 1.0 when ADP unknown

constructionNotes: thin starting slot: TE (Sam LaPorta, ADP 124.6)
teams.verdict: The cleanest board in the league: first in value captured, first in starting lineup, first in ceiling, first in bench. Stafford at 168 against an ESPN price of 86 was the draft's second-biggest value gap, and on the ESPN board the roster doesn't contain a single meaningful reach. When one team leads all four weighted categories, the letter writes itself.

picks.comment: The consensus 1.01, and he made it.
ESPN price 72.2, taken 73. No notes.
Priced at 86, drafted at 168. Only one value gap in the draft beat this one, and it plays tight end for Mustafa.

teams.verdict: A perfect construction score and no panicked picks. Henry at his exact market number and Burrow at 7.07 anchored a draft that paid a small premium at tight end and never once panicked. Docked to A- for the thin backfield behind Henry and the Allgeier reach. Otherwise this was textbook.

picks.comment: ESPN priced him at 17.8. Taken at 18. The machine approves.
A seven-pick premium for the tight end edge. Defensible.
Seven past price. Previously advertised here as grand larceny; downgraded to sensible shopping.

teams.verdict: Best backfield drafted, a real WR1, and a perfect construction score. The B+ instead of higher comes from a receiver room that thins out immediately after Nico Collins and a Rachaad White pick 37 ahead of price. Maye at 6.09 was strong quarterback timing. This roster is one trade from an A, and its manager said as much in the chat.

picks.comment: The quarterback timing everyone else wished they'd had.
Priced at 130. Thirty-seven picks early for a backup.
Fair price on the ESPN board, and immediately his WR3. That is the compliment and the problem.

teams.verdict: Second-best value capture on the board the model graded against, banked with late-round discipline: McMillan 23 past his ESPN price, the Patriots defense 14 past, Meyers at his number. The ceiling on the grade is what the value bought. The starting lineup scored ninth, with quarterback addressed at pick 118 and tight end acquired at a discount for a reason. Excellent shopping, modest pantry.

picks.comment: 49 picks ahead of ESPN's market. The one true reach.
12 past price. Reasonable value at the position he waited too long on.
23 picks past price in the final round.

teams.verdict: A top-heavy grade: Bijan and Pickens carried the ceiling score, and rounds 10 through 16 (Addison, Shakir, Nailor) rescued the value column on the board the model graded against. Between those bookends sat the shakiest RB middle in the draft, with Price 26 early and Kamara 38 early. Perfect construction, wobbly contents.

picks.comment: 26 picks ahead of price for the RB2 job this roster badly needed.
Priced at 160. A bet against the market's obituary.
20 past price in round 16. Free money.

teams.verdict: A market-clean draft with one big positional imbalance. Daniels came 36 past price and Warren at his market number; Brown and Egbuka ran a few picks hot. Seven receivers against three startable running backs cost construction points, and the ceiling rests on rookie receivers hitting. Balanced scores, no standout column, a straight B.

picks.comment: ESPN priced him at 19.7. Taken at 9. Aggressive, and no longer deniable.
Market price on ESPN's board. The model's old complaint didn't travel.
36 past price. Possibly the pick that ages best.
The RB depth plan, in its entirety.

teams.verdict: Elite starters at receiver and quarterback set against the weakest drafted starting backfield in the league. Goff at 188 (52 past price) and Hunter at 173 (53 past) were the two best pieces of late-round shopping. The B- is the average of an A top and a D backfield; no grading system splits that difference cleanly.

picks.comment: Asim's own review, in the chat, was that this pick might have "jacked up my roster." The model says it was market price.
55 picks ahead of price for a committee back. The desperation showed early.
52 past price. Exactly the insurance this roster needed.

teams.verdict: Remove one pick and this is a B+. Lloyd at 67 against an ESPN price of 166 was the draft's largest reach and sank the value column by itself. Hurts, Jeudy, and Ridley were quality timing. Graded exactly as drafted: eleven sound rounds and one that will be cited in this space all season.

picks.comment: Priced at 166. The largest reach in the draft by a wide margin.
A top-five quarterback at a discount.
19 past price. A coupon against the Lloyd invoice.

constructionNotes: thin starting slot: TE (Juwan Johnson, ADP 160.8)
teams.verdict: The first five rounds graded among the best in the league; the last eleven among the worst. Rodriguez (52 early) and Coleman (41 early) drained the value score, and a second quarterback in round 9 spent a pick the roster didn't owe. Cook insurance via Ray Davis was smart. C+ is the exact midpoint of two different drafts.

picks.comment: "He fell." ESPN priced him at 37; he went at 56. He fell. The desk stands corrected, publicly.
A second quarterback, taken directly in front of the one manager who needed one.
His own James Cook insurance. "I got my own cuffs."

teams.verdict: Last in value captured. Washington (57 early) and Keaton Mitchell (38 early) came at real premiums, while quarterback waited until pick 155. Lawrence at that price was excellent in isolation, but value on your own QB1 in round 13 is a symptom, not a plan. The young receiver core keeps this at C+.

picks.comment: 57 picks ahead of price. The sickness, documented.
60 past price. Great pick, alarming plan: this is the QB1.
The all-Jets endgame begins.

teams.verdict: The construction score, lowest in the league, tells the story: a round-nine kicker, a round-ten defense, and seven running backs without a locked starting job among them. St. Brown, Jefferson, and McBride was as good an opening three as anyone's. Eleventh in value, last in bench. The C averages a superstar draft with an org-chart problem.

picks.comment: With St. Brown already rostered: the league's best receiver duo, assembled by pick 15.
44 picks ahead of price, on the stated hope that "it's time."
ESPN says fair price. The desk says wrong aisle.

constructionNotes: thin starting slot: TE (Travis Kelce, ADP 119.9)
teams.verdict: Frozen in time, as promised: last in starting lineup, last in ceiling. Hampton ten early and Likely 40 early were premiums paid at exactly the wrong spots, while Kelce at 180 — the biggest value gap in the draft — pulled the value column back to mid-pack. The bench score is real consolation. The C- grades the lineup he has to start, not the one the chat believes in.

picks.comment: Ten picks ahead of price at 1.12. The market wanted him at the two-three turn.
40 ahead of price, at a position later solved for free.
84 past price — the largest value gap in the draft — while the chat spent ten minutes pricing in his wedding.

displayAdpSource.name: ESPN Live Draft Results
displayAdpSource.note: The league drafts in the ESPN app; this is the market the room drafted against. adpDiff = overall pick minus ADP: positive = drafted later than price (value), negative = earlier (reach).
